workstream: W4-1d — Inventory economic and business indicators
scope: Official Philippine Statistics Authority and City Government of Makati sources only. This step inventories usable GDP/economic-structure, labor-market, establishment and business-activity indicators; it does not implement indicator data.
geographyRule: For city economic series, treat 2022 as the Makati geography break unless a source explicitly restates earlier values to the current 23-barangay boundary. PSA PPA footnotes state that Makati figures exclude the Embo barangays starting in 2022.

officialSources.title: Provincial Product Accounts OpenSTAT tables
usableFor: GDP level at current and constant 2018 prices
HUC share of regional industry GVA
officialSources.geography: Province/HUC. PSA notes that Makati excludes the Embo barangays starting in 2022.
officialSources.note: Primary machine-readable owner for Makati GDP and industry series. Use 2022–2025 for a clean current-boundary trend unless a restated pre-2022 series becomes available.

officialSources.title: PSA Releases the 2025 Economic Performance of the 82 Provinces and 33 Highly Urbanized Cities
factsForValidation: Makati 2025 GDP: PhP 1.27 trillion at constant 2018 prices
Makati share of national GDP in 2025: 5.5 percent
officialSources.note: Use the OpenSTAT tables as canonical numeric series; use the release as a human-readable validation/context source.

officialSources.title: The City of Makati Posts 7.3 Percent Economic Growth in 2024, Tops Nation in Per Capita GDP
factsForValidation: 2023–2024 real GDP growth: 7.3 percent in the Makati release
officialSources.note: Useful validation/context for the existing city-comparison module and for industry-story labels.

officialSources.title: Gross Domestic Product by Province and HUC
officialSources.definition: GDP measures production of resident producers; HUC GDP is compiled using the production approach.

officialSources.title: Gross Domestic Product by Province and HUC, Growth Rates
officialSources.definition: Year-on-year rate of change in GDP.

officialSources.title: Gross Domestic Product by Industry, Province and HUC
officialSources.definition: Gross value added by 16 production industries; GVA equals gross output less intermediate consumption.
officialSources.note: Use this matrix for Makati industry levels. Derive each industry's share of Makati GDP explicitly; do not mislabel PSA's separate regional-industry-share table as Makati's internal industry mix.

officialSources.title: Gross Domestic Product Growth Rates by Industry, Province and HUC
officialSources.definition: Year-on-year growth rate of GVA by production industry.

officialSources.title: Gross Domestic Product Percent Share by Province and HUC
officialSources.definition: Share of a province/HUC GDP in its administrative region's GDP.
officialSources.note: This is a regional-share measure. It is not an industry-composition measure.

officialSources.title: Gross Domestic Product Percent Share by Industry, Province and HUC
officialSources.definition: Share of an industry's GVA in the HUC relative to the same industry's GVA in the region.
officialSources.note: Potentially useful for specialized economic-analysis reports, but too easy to misread as the industry's share of Makati's own economy. Do not use as the default Statistics composition measure.

officialSources.title: Per Capita Gross Domestic Product by Province and HUC
officialSources.definition: GDP divided by the relevant population denominator.
officialSources.note: Keep denominator metadata visible. The 2024 national comparison uses 2024 POPCEN population; the current OpenSTAT per-capita series notes use of preliminary 2020-based population projections for the relevant series.

officialSources.title: Highlights of the Labor Force Survey in the National Capital Region, 2025
officialSources.note: These are resident labor-market rates, not counts of jobs physically located in Makati. Label them accordingly.

officialSources.title: 2025 Regional Social and Economic Trends — total employed persons by city/municipality, 2019–2023
officialSources.note: Useful historical labor context, but the newer 2025 HUC labor-rate release is cleaner for the first Statistics batch. Do not confuse resident employed persons with workplace employment.

officialSources.title: 2021 Updating of the List of Establishments Final Result
officialSources.note: The reference year predates the current Makati/Taguig geography. Retain only as explicitly historical old-boundary context unless PSA publishes a restated current-boundary establishment series.

officialSources.publisher: Philippine Statistics Authority — NCR PSO III
officialSources.title: 2023 Census of Philippine Business and Industry and IOSPBI fieldwork for Makati, Pasig, Taguig and Pateros
usableFor: source discovery for future city business statistics
officialSources.note: The page reports a 7,337-establishment sample across four LGUs, not a Makati result. Never treat the fieldwork sample as Makati's establishment count. Revisit when Makati-level 2023 CPBI outputs are officially published.

officialSources.publisher: City Government of Makati — Urban Development Department
officialSources.title: Makati City Basic Facts and Figures 2023
usableFor: cooperatives and other city business-environment counts
officialSources.note: The city labels 86,370 as 'business establishments (per activity)'. That is not definitionally interchangeable with PSA's List of Establishments count. Preserve the city's wording and clarify unit/scope before implementation.

officialSources.title: Makati Facts and Figures 2020 — businesses
officialSources.note: Pre-transfer geography. Useful only as historical business-administration context; do not connect directly to 2023/current Makati as a continuous series.

candidateIndicators.period: 2022–2023 through 2024–2025 for the clean current-boundary series

candidateIndicators.period: 2025 headline; future series only if reproducible from canonical national/HUC data

Gross value added by Makati production industry at constant 2018 prices.
Year-on-year real GVA growth by Makati production industry.
Industry GVA divided by Makati total GDP for the same year/valuation basis.

candidateIndicators.definition: Makati industry GVA as a share of the same industry's GVA in NCR.
candidateIndicators.note: Specialist measure; not suitable as a default city economic-structure card.

candidateIndicators.definition: Makati GDP divided by the applicable population denominator.
candidateIndicators.period: 2024 census-based benchmark plus 2025 continuation with denominator metadata
candidateIndicators.note: Keep 2024's census-based comparison distinct from later projection-based values.

candidateIndicators.definition: Share of Makati residents age 15+ who are in the labor force.
Share of the Makati labor force that is employed.
Share of the Makati labor force that is unemployed.
Share of employed Makati residents who want additional hours or additional/new work with longer hours.
Annualized number of employed residents.

candidateIndicators.definition: PSA List of Establishments count for establishments physically located in Makati.
candidateIndicators.note: Do not use as a current Makati indicator because the reference year predates the territorial transfer.

candidateIndicators.definition: Employment reported by establishments physically located in Makati in the PSA List of Establishments.
candidateIndicators.note: Old-boundary historical measure and conceptually different from resident employment.

candidateIndicators.definition: City BPO count labeled 'No. of Business Establishments (per activity)'.
candidateIndicators.note: Needs a documented unit/denominator rule before use. Do not relabel it as distinct establishments.

candidateIndicators.definition: Operating PEZA-registered IT buildings reported in the city's Basic Facts and Figures.
candidateIndicators.note: Useful business-environment context, but lower priority than GDP/labor measures and should eventually cross-link to named assets only where an official facility list supports exact identity.

candidateIndicators.definition: Banks and other finance-related institutions reported by the city.
candidateIndicators.note: Category definition needs clarification before comparison or trend use.

candidateIndicators.definition: Makati establishment employment/revenue/expense/assets from the 2023 CPBI.
candidateIndicators.note: Wait for an official Makati-level published result; do not infer from the four-LGU sample count.

comparabilityRules: PPA values for Makati before 2022 and from 2022 onward must not be presented as one uninterrupted current-boundary series unless PSA publishes a restatement.
Use constant 2018 prices for growth/real-output trends; use current prices only when the user explicitly needs nominal values.
GDP per capita is economic output per resident, not household income, wages or personal wealth.
The 2024 per-capita comparison uses 2024 POPCEN population; later PPA per-capita values may use population projections and must carry denominator metadata.
Resident employment/LFPR/unemployment/underemployment measure Makati residents, not jobs or workers physically located in Makati workplaces.
PSA establishment employment and LFS resident employment are different concepts and must never share one label.
The city BPO 'business establishments (per activity)' count is not interchangeable with PSA's distinct establishment count.
A 2023 CPBI fieldwork sample spanning Makati, Pasig, Taguig and Pateros is not a Makati count.
Industry composition should be derived from Makati industry GVA divided by Makati GDP; PSA's industry regional-share measure answers a different question.
Missing or suppressed PPA industry cells remain unavailable; do not convert suppression into zero.

implementationBatchRecommendation.rationale: The first batch gives BetterMakati a current, well-defined city economy and resident labor-market picture using official sources with explicit current-boundary treatment. Business-establishment counts remain held or historical because the available city/PSA series do not yet form a clean current-boundary, definition-consistent trend.

crossFunctionReuse.use: GDP growth, industry structure and labor-market shifts are high-value report inputs, but reports should reference indicator IDs rather than duplicate the series.
Keep public-finance and city-economy measures distinct. Cross-link GDP/output context to fiscal records without implying city budget equals city economy.
Do not fabricate barangay GDP, employment or business counts from citywide data. Only barangay-scoped economic indicators with an official barangay denominator may be shown.
PEZA/business-building statistics may link to named canonical assets only when an official list proves exact identity. Never infer business density from mapped Place Registry records.

Use BetterGov national data/visualization tools for national GDP/industry context and BetterLGU/sibling sites for cross-LGU comparisons where a canonical destination exists; keep PSA or Makati official data as the visible source of record.

nextStep.title: Inventory service, land and infrastructure indicators
nextStep.maximumScope: Official-source research only; prioritize measures that connect to services, barangays, facilities or Place Registry records.
